newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia helps in search for hijacked tanker.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia helps in search for hijacked tanker.

text.p: Indonesia has pledged two aircraft to help in the search for a Malaysian gasoil tanker hijacked by pirates off the coast of Singapore last week, the official Antara news agency reported on Tuesday.
"We have already sent two aircraft to detect the whereabouts of the tanker," Rear-Admiral Achmad Sutjipto of the Indonesian navy was quoted as saying.
Achmad said two Australian-made Nomad N-22 aicraft were being deployed to search Indonesian waters for the tanker, which was hijacked last Tuesday by six pirates.
It was not yet known if the boat was in Indonesian waters, he added.

The Malaysian-owned vessel, Suci, and its $600,000 cargo of gasoil were stolen about 60 miles (100 km) off the east coast of Singapore while heading for Sandakan port in the Malaysian province of Sabah.

The hijacking came to light after 15 of the ship's 17 crew were rescued last Friday by a fishing boat operating from a port on the Indonesian island of Batam, about 50 miles (80 km) south of Singapore.
The 11 Indonesians, two South Koreans and two Burmese had been set adrift by the hijackers two days before.
A further two Indonesians, both engineers, were detained on board the ship by the pirates.
